accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The claimed degree-one correction is conditional on the separately stated pinned full-basis zero-remainder checkpoint and nonzero localized observable denominator.

source_verification_receipts.locator: PDF p. 5, Theorems 3.5--3.6 and accompanying proof
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.5 generically identifies the Fig. 3 proxy-to-treatment effect from the first k(l) cumulants; for l=1, Theorem 3.6 states nonidentifiability from the first three cumulants and reports that the effect is only a root of a degree-two polynomial in its Gröbner calculation.
The one-latent-component loading formula uses covariance and fourth-order cumulants under unit latent variance; it is not a cubic-only unknown-chain recovery theorem.

source_verification_receipts.version: author manuscript corresponding to Annals of Statistics 39 (2011)
source_verification_receipts.locator: Introduction and Section 3, especially discussion of generic versus global injectivity
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper distinguishes injectivity/global identifiability from generic injectivity and explains why exceptional fibers remain relevant.
The paper defines equivalence through equality of generated distribution sets and introduces quasi-equivalence for observational identifiability in linear Gaussian directed models.
LF-HTC is a sufficient criterion for rational recovery of direct effects from an observed covariance matrix in explicit-latent linear SEMs.
The paper supplies singularity-robust tests and confidence sets for moment-condition models under weak or absent identification.
